paper.title: Accurate and Robust Stellar Rotation Periods catalog for 82771 Kepler stars using deep learning

result.summary: 本文提出了 LightPred，一个结合 LSTM 与 Transformer 双分支架构的深度学习模型，用于从 Kepler 光变曲线中提取主序星的恒星自转周期 [abstract][S3.SS1.p2][S3.SS1.p3]。模型采用自监督对比预训练与基于模拟光变的监督训练两阶段流程 [abstract][S4.SS2.p1]。评估显示 LightPred 在准确率和平均误差上优于自相关函数（ACF）等经典方法 [abstract][S5.SS1.p2]。作者将模型应用于 Kepler 数据集，生成了迄今最大的自转周期目录，并基于学习到的置信度和一致性度量进行误差分析与筛选 [abstract][S5.SS3.p2]。分析还确认了轨道周期短于 10 天的食双星存在潮汐同步现象 [abstract][S5.SS2.SSS4.p5]。

research_question.text: 论文旨在解决从 Kepler 光变曲线中准确、稳健地测量大量恒星自转周期的问题 [S1.p1][S1.p3]。经典方法如 Lomb-Scargle 周期图和自相关函数虽然成功，但耗时且难以应用于大型数据集，并常难以处理具有多个周期或演化黑子模式的复杂光变曲线 [S1.p2]。作者指出，经典方法的一个缺点是难以提供预测的不确定性估计，而这对评估结果可靠性至关重要 [S1.SS1.p1]。

evidence.quote: The study of stellar rotation periods has become increasingly important in our understanding of stellar evolution, activity cycles, and exoplanet detection.
Classical methods for measuring rotation periods, such as Lomb-Scargle periodograms and autocorrelation functions, have been successful
but can be time-consuming and challenging to apply to large datasets.
Furthermore, these methods often struggle with complex light curves that exhibit multiple periodicities or evolving spot patterns.
In this paper, we present a novel deep-learning approach for measuring stellar rotation periods using Kepler light curves.
One shortcoming of classical methods is their inability to provide uncertainty estimates for predictions, which are essential for evaluating the reliability of the results.

method.text: LightPred 采用双分支架构：时序分支由卷积嵌入块、双向 LSTM 块和不可学习的自注意力块组成，输入为 Diff-ACF；全局分支基于修改的 AstroConformer，输入为 Diff-Lc [S3.SS1.p2][S3.SS1.p3]。两分支特征拼接后送入预测头，输出自转周期、倾角及各自的置信度分数 [S3.SS1.p4]。训练采用两阶段流程：先在 Kepler 样本上进行自监督对比学习（SSL），再以模拟数据集进行监督训练（SBSL） [S4.SS2.p1]。预处理包括截取 720 天光变曲线、注入 Kepler 噪声、Savitzky-Golay 滤波、计算差分光变曲线（Diff-Lc）及其自相关函数（Diff-ACF） [S2.SS2.p1]。

evidence.quote: Temporal branch - consists of an ”embedding” convolution block with max pool, dropout, batch normalization, skip connection, a bi-directional LSTM block, and a non-learnable self-attention block.
Global branch - here we follow the recent work of called Astroconformer.
The input of this branch is Diff-Lc.
The features from the two branches are concatenated and sent into the prediction head
The output of the model is four numbers: rotation period, inclination, period confidence score, and inclination confidence score.
To train the model, we used a 2-step pipeline; First, we trained the model, without the prediction head, in a self-supervised fashion, with Kepler samples.
Next, we used the weights from the SSL Step as an initialization for supervised training with the mock dataset.
We pre-processed each sample in the following way: First, we cut the first 200 days to reach a steady state for spot evolution.
Then we randomly chose a 720-day subset of the light curve (corresponding to 8 quarters of Kepler data).
We then applied a Savitzky-Golay filter with a window of 13 time-points ( $6h$) and created a time series of differences between consecutive time stamps to reduce long-term variations.
Next, we calculated the ACF of the Diff-Lc with all possible lags and filled missing values by linear interpolation.

experiments.text: 作者使用 Butterpy 生成的模拟光变曲线进行监督训练，模拟参数包括黑子涌现/衰减、纬度和经度分布等 [S2.SS1.p1]。训练集包含 50000 个模拟样本，按 81%/9%/10% 划分为训练、验证和测试集 [S4.SS2.p1]。在模拟数据上，作者将 LightPred 与 ACF 和 GPS 方法进行比较，评估指标为 10% 和 20% 误差范围内的准确率以及平均绝对误差 [S5.SS1.p1][S5.SS1.p2]。在 Kepler 数据上，模型对 130868 个样本进行预测，经过滤后得到 108096 个样本用于误差分析 [S5.SS2.p1][S5.SS2.SSS1.p1]。作者还进行了消融实验，比较完整模型、无差分预处理、仅时序分支、仅 Conformer 分支以及仅预测周期等变体 [S4.SS3.p1]。

evidence.quote: To create a dataset for supervised training we used simulated light curves using Butterpy, a python package described in.
This was done on a dataset of 50000 simulated samples of 1000 days that were generated as explained in II.1 and II.2.
We then split the dataset into training ( $81\%$), validation ( $9\%$), and test sets ( $10\%$).
We also adopted the same metrics - the percentage of samples that lie within 10% error ( acc10p) and the percentage of samples that lie within 20% error ( acc20p).
In addition, we used the average absolute error in days ( mean_err).
We compare our results to the results reported by the Tel-Aviv team in.
This left us with 130868 which serves both for the SSL step and the inference.
Out of the 130868 predictions we filtered out stars with $Teff<7000K$ which gave us 126029 samples.
this leaves us with 108096 samples.

the different models we tested are: 1. LightPred: The full model as shown in III.1. 2. LightPred no-diff: The same as LightPred with a change in the pre-processing; instead of using Diff-Lc and Diff-ACF, we used the regular light curve and ACF. 3. Temporal Branch: Using only the Temporal branch; LSTM-based network with Diff-ACF as input. 4. Conformer Branch: Using only the Conformer branch; a convolution-transformer network with Diff-Lc as input. 5. LightPred period only: the same as LightPred but without inclination predictions.

findings.text: 在模拟数据上，LightPred 在噪声和无噪声样本上的表现均优于 ACF 和 GPS 方法 [S5.SS1.p2]。在有效预测子集上，ACF 的 acc10p 和 acc20p 与 LightPred 相当，但 LightPred 的平均误差显著更低 [S5.SS1.p2]。模型输出的置信度与绝对误差呈负相关，表明模型能识别较难预测的样本 [S5.SS1.p3]。在 Kepler 数据上，LightPred 的观测误差分布比 ACF 更集中，在全部样本上误差更低；在 ACF 有效样本上两者误差相当，LightPred 略低 [S5.SS2.SSS2.p2]。自监督预训练显著改善了 Kepler 数据上的观测误差（约降低 3 倍） [S5.SS2.SSS2.p3]。分析食双星确认了轨道周期短于 10 天的系统存在潮汐同步 [S5.SS2.SSS4.p5]。最终目录包含 82771 个可靠预测 [S5.SS3.p2]。

evidence.quote: It can be seen that our results are better for both noisy and noiseless samples.
For a subset of valid predictions, we see that the performance of ACF is comparable to our model in terms of acc10p and acc20p but our model shows significantly lower average error.
The trend of high confidence and low error, which can be easily seen in the figure, implies that the model was able to infer which samples are ”harder” for it to determine the stellar properties.
Our model shows more concentrated distributions and when considering the entire samples (left panel), our model has much lower error.
When considering only ACF-valid samples (right panel), The errors are comparable, with LightPred error slightly lower than ACF error.
We see that self-supervised training improves all the metrics both on simulation and Kepler data.
While the improvement on simulation metrics is modest, the improvement on Kepler data is significant ( $\sim 3$ times lower observational error).
For $3<P_{orb}<10$, sp samples are very close to the synchronization line (the gray line at $P_{orb}/P_{rot}=1$) as expected.
This procedure left us with 82771 reliable predictions.

limitations.text: 作者指出，模拟模型存在倾角与黑子位置之间的内在简并性，且模型依赖先验分布，黑子分布对结果影响很大 [S2.SS1.p1]。对于周期大于 25 天的恒星，模拟误差与观测误差的相关性不同，可能与较老恒星活动性下降有关 [S5.SS2.SSS1.p2]。模型对极快自转体（周期 < 3 天）存在局限，在食双星分析中表现为同步线消失 [S5.SS2.SSS4.p5]。在周期不一致样本中，模型有时会错误地检测到真实周期的一半 [S5.SS2.SSS5.p3]。作者还指出，对于光变曲线周期性发生剧烈变化的样本，模型通常给出“平均”预测，而 ACF 仅检测高振幅区域的周期，哪种结果更好尚不明确 [S5.SS2.SSS5.p3]。

evidence.quote: The suggested model implies an inherent degeneracy between inclination and spot location.
This implies that the model is prior-depended: the distribution of spots in the model has a large effect on the results.
For longer periods the correlation is different which might be related to a drop in the activity for older stars.
For $P_{orb}<3$ Days and $P_{orb}>10$ Days we do not see synchronization.
While the latter is expected, the former can be assigned to the limitations of the model with very fast rotators, exactly as we saw in Figure 9.
In our visual inspection, we did find such examples where our model falsely detects half of the true period.
ACF would detect periods related to the high amplitude region only, regardless of its length, while our model usually gives a sort of ’average’ prediction.
It is not clear which result is better in general.
